punchline: Mice raised with no microbes at all developed asthma-like airway reactions to allergens, while mice with a full microbiota were protected.
thirty_sec: Stanford researchers Justin and Erica Sonnenburg describe mice raised with no microbes at all. You would expect them to be the healthiest animals around. But when an allergen is present, their airways react the way an asthmatic's do, while mice with a full microbiota are protected. The Sonnenburgs read this as a sign that gut bacteria help the body stay calm, and they add that much of the human evidence is still only observational.
